text:
Deepa: quick sync — dropping notes from the RFC follow-up on the operational handoff for quant profiles. want an action list by EOD :eyes:
Sam: thanks — can you summarize the main gap we identified in the rfc?
Deepa: main gap = runtime <-> ops contract for per-tenant overrides and a cheap signal that says 'prefer-quality' vs 'prefer-cost'. no one agreed on shape of that signal.
Leo: is that the same as the quality_budget we prototyped? seemed promising but messy w/ caching.
Deepa: yes. quality_budget was the prototype. problems: 1) cache key explosion (per-budget) 2) telemetry sparsity for small tenants 3) fallback semantics unclear under burst.
Maya: ops ask: how does this interact with canarying? we need deterministic routing so canaries get stable config.
Sam: proposal: two-layer approach — (A) short-lived hint header (X-Qual-Budget: low|med|high) used by runtime to pick profile, but not part of cache key; (B) immutable serving profile id used for cache/content-key. runtime maps hint -> profile id via per-tenant policy service.
Leo: that avoids cache explosion. but if mapping changes mid-request, how do we ensure KV cache compatibility?
Deepa: runtime will pin profile id at request start. mapping changes affect subsequent requests only. include a simple stamp: profile_id + schema_version in cache key.
Maya: good. what about telemetry? we need signals to decide if a profile is degrading quality.
Sam: telemetry plan: track short-window cohorts (by profile_id) with metrics: nll_delta, exact_match_rate on eval set, and downstream user visible regressions. surface a 95th-percentile rollback trigger.
Deepa: also add synthetic smoke runs every hour: shadow-requests sampled from production routed to fp32 baseline and lowbit candidate. compare logits delta distribution. if KL_divergence > threshold -> flag.
Leo: thresholds? ops wants concrete numbers to alert on.
Maya: propose a simple table to start: KL > 0.07 (warning), KL > 0.12 (critical), nll_delta mean > 0.05 -> critical. can refine later.
Sam: note: these are coarse. different models (chat vs code-gen) need different baselines. put model-tag in the telemetry dims.
Deepa: fallback semantics: if candidate profile triggers critical alert or runtime OOM/quant-failure, automatically fallback to next-safe profile id (precomputed chain). avoid hard crash.
Leo: chain example: fp8 -> int8 -> int4 -> fp16. but int4 often fails on longctx. need per-model chain.
Maya: ops needs a concise ops playbook for oncall: include commands to list profile statuses, force-promotion/demotion, and revert mapping.
Deepa: added a minimal ops cli:
```
# list
redwood quant profiles status --model t5-large
# force profile
redwood quant profiles set-mapping --tenant acme --model t5-large --profile fp32-v2
```
Sam: add audit log events for mapping changes and automatic fallbacks. compliance asked for that.
Maya: rollout plan? how do we pilot without risking customer experience?
Deepa: pilot steps: 1) shadow sampling on 5% traffic for 48h; 2) staged canary: 0.5% traffic for one customer cohort with manual approval; 3) expand to 10% with automated rollback enabled.
Leo: what about cost accounting? a customer with prefer-quality might burn tokens on fp32 — we need clear billing labels.
Sam: attach profile billing tags to requests and show line-item in console. ops also wants a guardrail: per-tenant budget cap that forces downgrade when exceeded.
Deepa: UX note: console should show "effective profile id" and the hint->mapping so support can triage.
Maya: open question: should customers be able to pin profile_id directly? legal/security might not like direct pins for hosted tier.
Sam: suggestion: allow pinning only for Dedicated/Private, hosted can request quality_budget and submit support ticket for pin.
Deepa: action items:
- Deepa: spec draft for runtime mapping API + cache-key stamping (PR by Wed)
- Sam: telemetry dashboard skeleton + initial thresholds (PR + dashboard link by Thu)
- Leo: implement profile chain config and safe-fallback handling in runtime (WIP)
- Maya: ops playbook + CLI commands + RBAC plan (doc by Fri)
- ops-bot: record the follow-up ticket in #incidents if automatic rollback triggers in prod
ops-bot: noted. created ticket INC-2026-1042 for 'quant auto-rollback observed' and subscribed @Maya @Sam @Deepa
Maya: thanks — will start drafting the oncall runbook and share in #eng-oncall.
Sam: one more: we should put a small, deterministic noise budget when mapping hint->profile for fairness so noisy tenants don't oscillate mapping every minute. e.g. only re-evaluate mapping every 5m unless critical.
Deepa: agreed. and log mapping changes with TTL to help debug.
Leo: ok — I can pair with Sam on the telemetry dims tomorrow.
Maya: bumping for visibility — tagging @Leo @Sam @Deepa for follow-ups. :thumbsup:
Deepa: thanks all. closing thread — will post the spec PR link here when it's open.
